title: ValueError
summary: The right type, but a value that makes no sense — the standard error for failed validation and parsing.
description: Contrast with `TypeError`, which means the wrong *kind* of thing. `int('abc')` is a ValueError: str is an acceptable argument type, 'abc' is not an acceptable value.

parameters.name: *args
parameters.description: Usually a message explaining what was expected.

examples.title: Where it comes from
examples.output:
ValueError - invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'
ValueError - 9 is not in list

examples.title: Raising it from your own validation

real_world_usage: Validating function arguments, parsing user input, and rejecting a malformed record at the boundary rather than deep inside.

common_mistakes.mistake: Raising TypeError for a bad value
common_mistakes.fix: TypeError is for the wrong type. A negative quantity is a ValueError.
Include what was expected and what arrived. 'invalid input' costs the next debugger an hour.

common_mistakes.mistake: Catching ValueError around a whole block
common_mistakes.fix: You lose which conversion failed. Wrap the single call.

security_notes: Validation messages are shown to users more often than any other error, so keep them descriptive about the *input contract* and silent about internals.
